# IMP-018 deterministic prerequisite contract 1

Architecture compatibility is **0.5**. Contracts/IR, Jobs, Leases, artifacts and persisted world record schemas remain **1**. This is a compatible bounded dependency-proposal API; it introduces no persistent work ledger, planner, worker-selection policy, recipe executor or crafting primitive.

`Prerequisites.Need` binds an existing guarded Job responsibility, original trusted principal/world/domain, typed capability arguments, material ID, positive integral quantity and allocation policy. A material requirement is distinct from the job's attributable-delivery completion predicate. Existing stock can satisfy a material requirement but cannot manufacture crop-delivery evidence or complete its Job.

`DeterministicPrerequisiteResolver.resolve` accepts immutable installed recipe/production snapshots, scope-approved current free-supply inspections, the existing capability-resolver selection port, current access policy and an explicitly cumulative parent `Budgets.Ledger`. It returns an immutable issued `Proposal`: typed resolution status/reason/qualification, stock-use proofs (including observed zero), stable production IDs, exact batches/output/surplus/remainders, dependency edges, producer-to-demand unit intents, original owners, current selected method references, and measured work/context bytes. Rejections retain performed counters and discard all proposed work/credits. Ports have no model, planner, effect, lease-acquisition or job-write authority.

Expansion uses available approved stock first. It checks every multiplication/addition and uses integral ceiling division; fractions, overflow, impossible quantities, unknown supply, unloaded targets and stale observations are explicit refusals. Remainders and surplus are proposed quantities, not observed stock or completion receipts. Catalog absence never invents an acquisition method. An installed recipe without registered physical support is `UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME/UNSUPPORTED_PRIMITIVE`; ordinary shortages or an existing-method gap remain reasoned blockages without research.

Coalescing requires identical outcome capability, actor, original principal/world/domain, source, destination, all other static arguments, material and allocation policy. Quantity alone may differ. Each root is independently checked against current visibility/control. Global physical-supply pools prevent incompatible requests from spending the same observed units twice. Shared subgraphs carry explicit unit intents; batch surplus is never allocated beyond actual output. Failed alternatives restore disposable builders/stock/intents, while visited nodes, edges, attempts and work remain consumed. Active-path cycles and later Jobs graph mutations are checked independently.

Production `KernelSession.resolvePrerequisites` uses `FabricPrerequisiteRuntime.resolve`: current caller read/control, exact responsibility/guard/state and original bindings are checked before private supply is inspected. Expansion and admission/billing occur in one bounded game-thread operation, so repeated requests cannot reset the existing Job's remaining allowance. Pending publication blocks another expansion. The pure engine's independently supplied Ledger remains cumulative across repeated calls.

`PrerequisiteAdmission.submit` revalidates the current installed catalog, every root, every consumed or zero-stock proof, current lease conflicts/source identities, and selected existing method/bindings/fresh observation. Stock appearing, disappearing, changing identity or losing access returns a qualified stale/authority refusal. Revalidation and expansion are charged through Jobs' existing durable instruction usage; a billing refusal is exposed explicitly. `JobLifecycleStore.admitPrerequisites` atomically publishes existing schema-1 child Jobs, owned-child links, dependencies and budget usage, with finite current allowances and the original deadline. The root owning a shared producer pays its execution through existing ancestry; additional demand roots are dependencies/credit consumers, not extra allowance sources. No model bytes, repairs or trials are granted to prerequisite children. `CALLS` remains available for existing primitive invocation, which uses the same counter.

Current executable production is the existing `CropDelivery` wheat mapping. Non-wheat/future crafting accounting is explicitly unsupported for Jobs admission. The generic immutable graph/recipe contract is exercised by fake registered-production fixtures; these do not claim Minecraft crafting ability. `FabricPrerequisiteCatalog.capture` reads at most eight caller-selected exact installed keys via Minecraft's RecipeManager. It supports bounded ordinary static shaped/shapeless layouts and common exact remainders, rejects dynamic/component/alternative-dependent shapes conservatively, and never enumerates all recipes, assembles items or changes inventory. The native bread recipe is an unsupported-physics witness. No duplicate Minecraft recipe encyclopedia is embedded.

`ResourceLeaseService.inspectWithEvidence` returns the observation from the same current read-only inspection that subtracts authoritative claims. `LeasePrerequisiteSupplies` supports the already implemented wheat-container and mature-crop resource bindings. Observed empty approved stock is known zero; stale, unloaded, denied or invalid targets are never normalized to zero. Inspections acquire no claims. Execution continues to acquire/revalidate existing leases through `LeasedGateway`.

Only `Jobs.allocate` records output credit, using a terminal attributable deposit receipt, current demand guard/scope, existing batch/receipt/demand totals and an additional producer/demand maximum. `PrerequisiteAdmission.allocate` supports separate native receipts, stable per-demand/producer/attempt/receipt allocation IDs and explicit portions. Existing intent, stock, remainder or surplus is never credit. Allocation replay is idempotent; a changed quantity on the same receipt ID is refused. Root `fulfilled()` retains attempt credit; shared-output credit stays in Jobs' existing allocation records and can complete the root's state.

Stable production IDs omit quantities and transient observation/catalog IDs. Replay of an issued proposal returns a duplicate without minting children, renewing deadlines or refunding usage. Fresh re-expansion uses `submitExpanded` and charges performed work even when producer IDs are duplicates. Method selection includes the existing resolver decision plus bounded extra supply-inspection work, so native revalidation is metered without changing IMP-028 counters. A changed proposal that conflicts with equivalent work linked through a root's children or dependencies is stale, including a changed canonical owner when the previous owner is absent from the new cohort. It cannot mint another producer or silently replace responsibility. Cancellation/failed work cannot reactivate. Retry uses existing Job lifecycle operations and retained receipt credit. Disposable proposal state is never reconstructed as executable authority on reload; schema-1 JobJournal/ResourceLeaseJournal recovery and compatibility rules continue to own saved state and inactive lease epochs.

| Bound | Default and hard ceiling |
|---|---|
| Root demands | 8 |
| Visited production nodes, including failed alternatives | 16 |
| Expansion depth | 4; actual Jobs admission also enforces its existing root-inclusive depth |
| Dependency/input edges | 64 |
| Alternatives per production/input choice | 4 default, 8 maximum; total attempts also consume the 512-work envelope |
| Expansion plus runtime admission work | 512; every repeated operation also consumes remaining parent instructions |
| Renderable proposal context | 16,384 UTF-8 bytes |
| Quantity | 4,096 default, 1,000,000 maximum; actual P0 request output remains 1..64 |
| Current observation age | 10 ticks; authoritative lease inspection keeps its existing production freshness rule |
| Immutable source catalog | 128 recipe rows, 32 registered mappings, 8 ingredients/remainders per row, 16 item alternatives, 128-character IDs |
| Native recipe selection | 8 exact keys, 9 placement slots; no broad registry scan |
| Physical supply inspection | Existing lease owner: 256 cells/work per observation |
| Durable jobs/edges/allocations | Existing Jobs/Leases settings, byte bounds, guards, journals and publication deadlines |

No schema migration or new recovery file is required. Existing IMP-015/016 compatibility and retention continue to apply to Jobs, leases and pinned execution artifacts. Scratch catalogs/proposals carry no retention authority.
